consent.title: Data protection and privacy
consent.intro: Before you continue, please read how SOLIDARIS uses your personal information.
notice: The SOLIDARIS team collects your name, email address, institution, position, country and discipline, the projects you take part in, your role on each project, and the work you record (evidence, ratings, comments, decisions).
We use this information only to run the platform: to manage your account, coordinate projects, keep an accountable record of assessment decisions, and contact you about your projects.

Your information is stored with our hosting provider (Supabase) in the United Kingdom. It is visible only to you, the members of projects you join, and authorised administrators. Every change to project records is kept in an audit log.

We handle personal information in line with the data protection laws that apply to our partners, including the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, the EU and UK General Data Protection Regulation, and Canada's Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA).

You can ask for a copy of your personal information or ask us to delete it. If you leave, we anonymise your personal details but keep the audit record of project decisions, which research integrity requires.
consent.processing: I agree that SOLIDARIS may collect and use my personal information to run my account and the projects I take part in.
consent.handling: I understand my information is stored securely for this purpose, is visible to my project teams and administrators, and that project decisions are kept in an audit log.
consent.email: Send me email notifications about my projects (invitations, reviews, decisions). You can turn this off at any time.
consent.draftNote: This notice is awaiting legal review before public launch.

roleHelp.pi: Leads the project: builds the team, records most gate decisions and approves the final profile.
roleHelp.assessor: Rates the nine domains independently, with evidence. Cannot see other assessors' ratings until the comparison stage.
roleHelp.reviewer: Checks quality and completeness. Recommends revisions but never changes ratings.
roleHelp.observer: Read-only. Sees the profile and reports once they are validated.
roleHelp.external_expert: Gives specialist advice: reviews evidence and joins deliberation.
roleHelp.kt_lead: Takes the profile to decision-makers and records how it is used.
roleHelp.community_participant: Represents affected communities in deliberation and sees the validated profile.

subjectTypeHelp.programme: A set of linked activities run under one plan.
subjectTypeHelp.portfolio: A group of holdings, each profiled on its own and shown side by side — never combined.
subjectTypeHelp.investment: A funding commitment or financial instrument.
subjectTypeHelp.policy: A law, regulation, strategy or official policy.

gate.title: Gate {{gate}} review

purpose.G0: Is the subject in scope, with a named decision and a clear human-rights screen?
purpose.G1: Is the context understood, the team in place, and community voice planned?
purpose.G2: Is there enough evidence, or documented gaps, for every domain?
purpose.G3: Have all assessors submitted complete, independent assessments?
purpose.G4: Are the integrity checks, risk flags and solidarity type complete?
purpose.G5: Have divergent ratings been discussed, with consensus or dissent recorded?
purpose.G6: Has the profile been quality-assured and checked with affected stakeholders?
purpose.G7: Has the profile reached the decision-maker, with a response recorded?
purpose.G8: Have actions been followed up, signals reviewed and reassessment decided?

glossary.gate: A checkpoint between stages. The gate owner reviews a checklist and records a decision; the project moves on only through that decision.
glossary.conditionalGo: Move to the next stage now, with written conditions. Each condition is tracked and checked again at the next gate.
glossary.hold: Stay at the current stage until the problems are fixed. The reason is recorded and the gate can be reviewed again.
glossary.stopRedirect: Close the project with a recorded reason — for example when a subject is escalated rather than profiled.
glossary.hrScreen: A first check that the subject does not involve flagrant human-rights violations. If it does, the case is escalated instead of profiled.
glossary.coi: Any financial, professional or personal link to the subject that could affect, or seem to affect, your judgement.
glossary.actorMap: The funders, implementers, community actors and government bodies involved, with their influence and level of participation.
glossary.communityVoice: How the people the subject affects take part in the assessment.
glossary.singleAssessor: A profile made by only one assessor. It is allowed, but labelled Exploratory and cannot be marked Validated.
glossary.autoCheck: Worked out from the data you have entered. You can add a note, but an automatic “No” cannot be overruled — fix the underlying information instead.
